_README: This is YOUR file, not the protocol's. It declares what should and should not
happen in YOUR building. Copy it, edit it, point the hub at it:
The two policies below are exactly what server.py used to hard-code into the
reference hub until 2026-07-14 — including the 00:00-06:00 window, which was
one household's choice that every other hub silently inherited. They are here
so nothing is lost: if you want that behavior, use this file. If you don't,
delete them. The reference hub now ships with NO deployment policies, because
the protocol has no opinion about your house.
A policy that fails to load STOPS THE HUB (unknown type, bad argument, missing
file). That is deliberate: a policy is usually a restriction, and a typo that
silently skipped one would leave you believing you are protected when you are

policies._why: Was hard-coded in server.py. One house's overnight window, inherited by every hub running the reference implementation.
policies.reason: Security policy: no remote unlocking between 00:00 and 06:00

policies._why: The mechanism for operator preference, from the QA-1b benchmark: a TV is genuinely display-capable (its manifest says so, truthfully) but this operator does not want screens involved in notifications. Capabilities are declared with the truth; preferences are expressed HERE. Never mutilate a tag to express a preference.
policies.reason: Operator preference: screens do not participate in notifications or emergencies
